rows.rule_name: Consumer Directed Resource Policy (board policy for loads greater than 50 MW, data centers included)

together, the board, staff, and member CEOs, developed a framework and policy for serving large megaloads, like data centers.

rows.utility: Seattle City Light (City of Seattle, City Light Department)
rows.iso_region: outside an ISO (Seattle City Light balancing authority, Western Interconnection)
rows.rule_name: SMC 21.49.059 New large data center load: a new data center customer class served only under a Service Agreement (Council Bill 121231, passed as Ordinance 127473, the 2027-2028 retail rate ordinance)
rows.source_title: Council Bill 121231 v2 (the version passed on 21 July 2026 as Ordinance 127473): an ordinance relating to the City Light Department; establishing new retail rate schedules; establishing a new customer class and conditions of service for data centers (seattle.legistar.com)

quoted_clause.quote: 21.49.059 New large data center load A. Applicability. A new large data center load shall not be eligible for general service rates and shall instead be served under a Service Agreement (Contract) established for the customer by the Department.

cites.quote: Our New Large Data Center Load Policy was adopted, and effective immediately, as part of our rate ordinance in July 2026.
7/21/2026 2 City Council passed Pass
This ordinance shall take effect as provided by Seattle Municipal Code Sections 1.04.020 and 1.04.070, except that Sections 10 and 12 shall take effect on January 1, 2027.

status.note: passed by the City Council on 21 July 2026 and signed by the Mayor on 22 July 2026 (the legislation history); City Light says the policy took effect immediately; the class covers capacity installed after 1 January 2027 (the definition)

threshold_mw.value: 10 MVA or more of new or expanded data center capacity installed within any consecutive five-year period after 1 January 2027 (stated in MVA, not MW)

cites.quote: "New large data center load" means any service to a data center fed from an expanded or a new installation equal to or greater than 10 MVA of capacity installed within any consecutive five-year period after January 1, 2027.
Applies to data centers with new or expanded service of 10 megavolt-amperes (MVA) or greater

min_demand.value: the contract must carry a guaranteed minimum demand or service rating (level set in each contract, not in the ordinance); demand is billed on contract demand, and demand above it is charged at 300 percent of the demand charge

cites.quote: The Contract shall require all the following terms, among other conditions: 1. A guaranteed minimum demand or service rating.
The demand for billing purposes is the contract demand, unless otherwise specified.
Contract demand overrun charge = metered demand in excess of the contract demand (kW) x demand charge ($/kW) x 300 percent.

contract_term.value: not exceeding 20 years (City Light's authority to sign data center contracts for new large loads)

cites.quote: The Department is authorized to execute contracts with data center customers to serve new large loads pursuant to Section 21.49.059 for an effective term not exceeding 20 years.

collateral.value: full upfront financial responsibility for the cost of any infrastructure needed to serve the customer; the contract may add other terms for security and financial risk (no amount stated)

cites.quote: Full upfront financial responsibility for the cost of any infrastructure needed to serve the customer
Any other terms of service needed to address transactional costs, security, and financial risk.

exit_fee.value: no exit fee is named; the customer stays fully responsible for the cost of the agreements City Light signed to serve its load until the contract term expires

cites.quote: The customer shall remain fully responsible for the cost of agreements executed by the Department to serve the customer's load, until the expiration of the Contract term.

study_timeline.searched: CB 121231 v2 Section 7 (SMC 21.49.059, pp. 40-42) and Section 14 (p. 59); the Summary and Fiscal Note (p. 4); City Light's post of 12 June 2026 (updated for July 2026); City Light Review Panel minutes of 4 May and 17 June 2026

connection_timeline.searched: CB 121231 v2 SMC 21.49.059 C (p. 41) states a condition, not a time: "Service to new large loads will commence only after a Contract has been fully executed and the Department has in place all infrastructure, contracts, and resources necessary to provide electrical service."; City Light's post and the Summary and Fiscal Note give no time either

queue_size.value: five proposed large data centers from four companies, combined maximum demand 369 MW (approaches to City Light reported in April 2026, as the City Council's release of 9 June 2026 states)

cites.quote: follow reports in April that four companies had approached Seattle City Light to build five large-scale data centers. These proposed facilities would have a combined maximum demand of 369 megawatts

queue_size.note: the City Council (the utility's rate-setting body) states the figure, citing reports in April; it is a count of approaches, not of signed service requests

rows.license_basis: the City of Seattle's legislative record (seattle.legistar.com) and City web pages; seattle.gov's terms of use (https://www.seattle.gov/digital/terms-of-use, read 13 November 2026) set no limit on use or reproduction
rows.notes: The signed Ordinance 127473 PDF (legistar2.granicus.com) is refused by robots; the text read is the passed version 2 of the bill on seattle.legistar.com (the history shows version 2 passed by the Council on 21 July 2026 after the committee's amendment of 15 July). Other conditions of SMC 21.49.059: curtailment provisions and energy conservation measures (B.5, B.6), full recovery of the procurement cost of new resources (B.8), energy and demand charges at City Light's marginal cost plus a service fee (D.1). City Light's own summary: threshold "10 megavolt-amperes (MVA) or more" (post); the Review Panel minutes of 17 June 2026 (p. 2) say "greater than 10 MVA". Separately, the City Council's one-year moratorium (Council Bill 121214) bars siting data centers over 20 MVA within city limits; that is a land-use rule, not a connection rule. Corrected by the independent audit of session 5304 (A-07): was 'in effect 2026-07'. The City Council passed the ordinance on 21 July 2026 (Legistar history). City Light's post says the policy was 'adopted, and effective immediately' in July 2026, but the ordinance's Section 15 sets its effect by SMC 1.04.020 and 1.04.070, whose dates are not printed in the copies read, and the class reaches only capacity installed after 1 January 2027.

min_demand.searched: the Large Load Electric Service Agreement sections 1 to 14: no minimum demand or take-or-pay share (section 8 makes the member responsible for costs of "reduction in load below planned levels", see exit_fee); the request form, the Reimbursable Services Agreement and the Construction Development Agreement

contract_term.value: no fixed term: the Electric Service Agreement remains in effect until terminated

cites.quote: This Agreement shall remain in effect until terminated.

collateral.value: an irrevocable standby letter of credit kept for the whole term of service, amount set by the Cooperative (it may set minimums per MW or per MVA); 100 percent of the estimated construction cost (CIAC) paid within 10 business days of the Construction Development Agreement; a study deposit of $5,000 per MW of requested load, capped at $1,000,000

cites.quote: Member shall provide and maintain, at all times during the term of Service, an irrevocable standby letter of credit in favor of the Cooperative. The amount of the letter of credit shall be determined by the Cooperative
may establish minimum requirements on a per MW or per MVA basis
Within ten (10) business days of execution of this Agreement, Developer shall provide payment equal to one hundred percent (100%) of the estimated construction cost (CIAC).
an initial reimbursable deposit equal to Five Thousand Dollars ($5,000) per MW of requested load, as identified in the Electric Service Request, not to exceed One Million Dollars ($1,000,000).

exit_fee.value: no fixed fee: on termination all outstanding amounts fall due at once, and the member bears stranded transmission or distribution investment, underused or abandoned facilities, load below planned levels, decommissioning and any other unrecovered cost of serving it

cites.quote: Member shall be responsible for all costs associated with stranded transmission or distribution investments, underutilized or abandoned facilities, reduction in load below planned levels, decommissioning or retirement of facilities, and any remaining unrecovered costs associated with providing Service.
Upon termination of Service, all outstanding amounts shall become immediately due and payable.

study_timeline.searched: the request form and the Reimbursable Services Agreement: no study duration; the form sets only that a request expires 90 days after submission without an executed Reimbursable Services Agreement and initial payment (see notes)

connection_timeline.searched: the Electric Service Agreement section 1 states a condition, not a time ("Service shall commence only after completion of all required facilities, satisfaction of all contractual requirements, and authorization by the Cooperative."); the Construction Development Agreement gives no construction duration

rows.notes: Request form p.1: a request enters the "large load evaluation queue" only after the Reimbursable Services Agreement is executed and the deposit paid, and "A request for large load electric service will expire ninety (90) days after submission unless the Reimbursable Services Agreement has been executed" and the initial payment received; submission "does not establish queue position or priority for service". Electric Service Agreement section 4: $1,000 per installed MVA a month; energy at North Texas ERCOT real-time LMP plus a margin; 100 percent of transmission-related costs; bills may be weekly, due in 10 business days. The page links the form as large-load-electric-service-request-final-1.pdf; the copy read is large-load-electric-service-request-final.pdf in the same folder.
